data.reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, finding standard AUR packaging with pinned GitHub release sources and SHA-256 checksums. Report 1 (qwen3-235b) returned inconclusive solely due to an API error (HTTP 400) during the full PKGBUILD review, not due to security concerns. Notably, Report 1's initial PKGBUILD audit (which succeeded before the error) also found the file safe. The package contains only standard variable definitions, fetches from the project's own GitHub releases with checksum verification, and has no dangerous commands in global scope or suspicious build/install logic.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not substantive but mechanical: Report 1's full PKGBUILD review failed with an HTTP 400 API error, forcing an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 completed the same review successfully and found no issues. Both models' analyses that did complete (Report 1's initial audit and full .SRCINFO review; Report 2's full reviews of both files) agreed the package is safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in an inconclusive file verdict
learnings: When a full file review fails due to API/tool errors, the system should check whether an initial audit of that file succeeded and factor that into the overall verdict rather than defaulting to inconclusive
API errors should be distinguished from security findings in verdict aggregation - a tool failure is not evidence of risk
